utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Before we start, I would like to inform the parties that the B/C/S version of the written decision of the Appeals Chamber on the matters of assignment of the counsel is available. And the registrar has already given a copy to Mr. Blagojevic. If there's any problems on the part of Mr. Blagojevic, he could consult with his counsel, Mr. Karnavas, as well as the counsel in the registrar. The second issue is that on Thursday, 20th November we will only be sitting for two sittings and we stop at 12.00 sharp. Well, I think we could start. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Karnavas: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Butler.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to switch the topics a little bit now -- actually we're more or less on the same topic about your analysis. And I understand from your testimony that you have, indeed, rethought your position on one of the intercepts that I believe was generated on the 12th of July, an intercept that had -- that was between a certain general and a certain Jankovic. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think that's the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I apologise. And I've just been handed a note by my co-counsel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as I understand it, at the time that you testified during the Krstic trial, you did not have certain materials that became available after the Krstic trial, which in effect provided you with sufficient information for you to make a different conclusion. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that specific intercept, it was not until after the conclusion of the Krstic trial. So in that respect, you're correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, in fact, as I understand it, you or the Prosecutors were able to interview the individual -- or one of the individuals on the intercept. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe we interviewed both of the individuals, however I think if memory serves me correctly, the individual I believe we're talking about who is a protected witness was the only one that issue was addressed to. I do not believe it was addressed to the other person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now -- and it's your opinion -- so now we're pretty clear on this intercept at least. Now, I just want to walk you through what you said during Krstic, and then we're going to go through the intercept itself and discuss it, okay? So, if we could go to page 4.849 of the Krstic trial which was Wednesday, 28 June 2002. And if I could have Mr. Usher assist us here, we have something for the ELMO. It's fairly short. And I'll be reading all the way basically into the first line of 4.850. If you could just look at it first. If you look at the top of the page, you'll see it does mention your name, but if you want to give it a quick glance.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm familiar with this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The questions begins: "All right. Let's go now. Exhibit 449." And Mr. McCloskey says:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, 450. That is a July 13th conversation. Now we've come over on to the early morning of the 13th, 7.00 a.m. What can you tell us about this conversation?"

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This conversation occurs again early morning hours of 13 July. The correspondent X is looking for whom I believe the first indication of the name Nikolic, a Captain First Class Momir Nikolic, the chief of intelligence and security for the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you think that? Nikolic is a fairly common name.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, going into the aspect of the rest of the conversation, we now that Captain First Class Nikolic is, in fact, involved in dealing with the aspects of Muslim people in Potocari on both the 12th and the 13th. Additionally, he's specifically dealing with issues of Muslim wounded males in Bratunac on the 13th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, how about the reference to the other people there?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jankovic, I believe when we look at it in context with other material, the individual referred to is Colonel Radislav Jankovic, the chief or a member of the intelligence administration of the VRS Main Staff. We make that conclusion -- I make that conclusion insomuch as we have his involvement on the meetings with the 11th and the 12th, and we have other messages and orders by him showing his dealing with the actual movement of the population from Potocari out through to Kladanj. So we know that Colonel Jankovic is extremely well involved in this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I note in the middle of the page on this conversation that he is introduced as: "Here's police commander Jankovic." Would that be a MUP guy and not the Main Staff Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a possibility, yes, sir. Now, do you recall being asked those questions and do you recall giving those answers?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And so it would appear that at least you're certain about one positive identification of one of the individuals that is being mentioned, and that is Momir Nikolic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And in fact you give his rank as captain first class, though you may not be aware that there's only two classes and the first class is actually captain and the second class in their system is first class. Anyway, so we have one positive identification. Now -- and then there's a matter of who these other two gentlemen are, the ones that are speaking. Now, I want to focus on the individual who is named Jankovic. You've indicated that you believe this is the same Colonel Jankovic from the Main Staff. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I believe we've handed you and you have handy the intercept itself, what has been marked as Prosecution Exhibit 166/A, I guess. If you could look at it very quickly.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want it on the ELMO, sir?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You could put it on the ELMO, if you wish. And that is the intercept that we're discussing. Right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we flip to the second page, there's a question: "Where is Nikolic?" Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the gentleman indicates that he went home at half past 3.00. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me stop you here. At this point in time, it's clear that there is a conversation being placed to the command post of the Bratunac Brigade, is it not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And would it be correct that this conversation now is taking place between someone at the operations -- duty operations officer and whoever else is calling him at the time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it's the duty operations officer or some other correspondent in the Bratunac Brigade headquarters. So I couldn't say that, because it's not identified as such.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: But, yes, certainly within the confines of the Bratunac Brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And -- so you -- from this, you couldn't draw a conclusion or a supposition as to the possibilities of where this call would actually be to?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are a number of different options I would understand, the duty operations centre. I suspect that the assistant commander for security has his own phone line and a few other. I don't know the answer to that. Like I said, I don't know that we need to go any further. Certainly it's within the confines of the Bratunac Brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And from this intercept, it would appear that Nikolic isn't there because he's decided to go home and this person is filling in for him. Does it not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. In that respect, certainly the individual knows where Nikolic went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And so it would appear that Nikolic had left approximately 3.30 in the morning, because it said he left -- this takes place around 7.00 in the morning. And if we work our way backwards, it would appear that this individual -- that Nikolic left approximately 3.30 in the morning. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It testifies he went home, so yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He went home. So it would be safe to say, would it not -- or one of the possibilities is that this person is manning the phones in lieu of or instead of Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's a possibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And so if this were a conversation being placed to the operational duty officer, because obviously a lot of information is being asked at this time, it would appear then, would it not, that a captain from the brigade has left at 3.30 in the morning, and someone from the Main Staff, a colonel, is filling in for him. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't and I don't believe in my initial analysis I used the phrase "filling in for him". But certainly as part of my initial analysis on this, I did attribute that it was Colonel Jankovic and he was physically there, not filling in for him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And now, is that because you knew at the time that Jankovic was sharing offices with Nikolic, and therefore you automatically assumed that the conversation was or the call had been placed directly to Nikolic's office?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. The information at the time indicated that Jankovic, at least within the context of leadership within the VRS was a distinctive name with respect to Srebrenica 1995. In that particular issue, I understood, and at the time I learned later there was another Jankovic, the only Jankovic I knew was that of Colonel Radislav Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, assuming -- but let me ask you this: So you never entertained the thought in your analysis that this conversation could have been to the duty officer at the time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe that at the time that issue came up. With respect to who the -- where the context of the correspondents or the correspondents were, whether it was the duty officer or not, I don't believe that entered into the equation at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, you didn't think about that to say, "Well, maybe it's from the operation, they're calling in because they're trying to figure out what's going on." Right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is a possibility, but since in this particular intercept it doesn't identify either through voice compromise or some other piece of information identify whether it was the duty officer or the operations centre, it was not an issue that I wanted to speculate on. It wasn't of relevance with respect to the Krstic trial to my knowledge, whether it came into the duty officer or whether it was just within the broader confines of the Bratunac Brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, had you been to the Bratunac Brigade headquarters before?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I've never been to the Bratunac Brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware physically where Mr. Nikolic's, Captain Nikolic's, office was, either on the ground floor or the first floor? We would call it the second floor in the States?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure of the specifics. I would have to go back and review Captain Nikolic's first interview with the OTP. I don't recall that the actual physical layout was discussed in that first interview.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, in that first interview, if my memory serves me correct, there was no discussion with respect to this particular intercept, which mentions his name?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, there was not, to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that interview took place, as I believe, back in 1999, the first interview?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: December 1999, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And so -- but you would agree with me that one possibility of this phone call, since they're asking for information, would have been to the duty operation officer, because after all that's where all of the data is coming in, and this is 7.00 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. That's a valid interpretation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And if that's a valid interpretation, it would be sort of unreasonable to assume that a captain would have a colonel from the Main Staff come in and fill in for him?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly as the duty officer, I believe that is unreasonable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Because -- I mean, in fact it doesn't make any sense?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You would think that that particular colonel would have better things to do than fill in as the duty officer for a subordinate brigade, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Militarily, under the rules, it can't happen?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I don't think it can happen under their rules.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, even if it could happen, Nikolic would have to call his command, Colonel Blagojevic, in order to get permission for this to occur?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, there is one instance where you talked about the other Nikolic, Dragan Nikolic, how that happened in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Well, one of the questions that is being asked is: Who is up there? He says they're "up there" with respect to the boss in this particular intercept. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you give that any thought?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the context of believing that the correspondent was Colonel Jankovic, my assessment at the time on that was that the commander in question was General Mladic. I can go the next step now, knowing that it is, in fact, another Jankovic, in that respect the commander that they would be talking about should be Colonel Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Assuming that up there means physically up there?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does indicate in the next one with the men from up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Okay. Now, you're given another chance to speculate, if I can use that word, or provide us with another possibility, and you're asked: Well, could it be -- the question is posed, somewhat leading in nature, but never mind. I note in the middle of the page on this conversation that he's introduced as: "He's police commander Jankovic." Correct? That would be on, I believe, the first page.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I've got it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And then the -- it goes on and this is the leading part, which I would have objected to. "Would that be a MUP guy and not a Main Staff Jankovic?" In other words giving you an opportunity now to make a choice. And you say: "It is a possibility, yes, sir." In other words, a possibility that a MUP now, somebody in the MUP would be there, manning the phones or answering a phone where one would expect to find Momir Nikolic on that particular day. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't take it as such. I believe that the context of the question was the identification of police commander Jankovic, would that be an individual with the MUP and not the Main Staff Jankovic. I don't believe I took it to the next part of your conclusion, which was that it would be logical to assume that a MUP guy is answering the phone for Nikolic. I just left it at the point where are we talking about an individual from the VRS or are we talking about an individual who could be from the MUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Correct. But this call is being placed to the Bratunac Brigade headquarters someplace, and it would appear from the -- it would appear from the question that you're being asked whether that person is sitting in, giving information about Nikolic, and that person happens to be a commander of MUP. That's how I read it. How do you read it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That's a misconstruction of the answers, that's a misconstruction of the testimony. There needs to be a factual basis of some sort to a question that's asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How do you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you read this question posed to you by the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I explained, the way that I read this question is that: Is the identification of police commander Jankovic an individual who is a MUP person or is an army - or a Main Staff in this case - person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you say it's a possibility, yes?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'm trying to ask, because obviously that was something that was expected -- this was a question expected of you to answer. How is it that you thought that MUP, a commander of MUP, would be answering a phone in the Bratunac Brigade headquarters where one would find Momir Nikolic? What led you to that conclusion to say yes, that's a possibility? Because you could have gone on and said, that's a possibility, but I rule it out and here are the reasons why.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I raise the issue that it was a possibility because, particularly, trying to do the analysis on the basis of intercepts and other information, I'm not there. It is a possibility and it's not one that I'm prepared or at the time I was prepared to exclude. So I hold open the fact that there is an alternative possibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a reason why when you interviewed Momir Nikolic when you had him, that -- do you know whether -- why he was never asked that question?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why he was never asked to discuss this intercept?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to his first interview, I don't think I'll be going out on a limb by saying that he was being very economical with the truth, and, in fact, most of the information he provided in that first interview was information we came back and determined to be patently false.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: So given the fact my understanding of the way the situation was, given the fact that he was just being completely untruthful, the decision was, basically we'll take the information we have at the interview and move from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you weren't interested in maybe asking him who could this Jankovic be that said you left three and a half hours earlier on July 13th, that you were just totally disinterested in?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I was extremely interested. However, the practical reality at the time was we weren't going to get very many truthful answers out of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did ask him about the 65th Protection Regiment, right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, and if I recall correctly he knew almost nothing about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He gave an explanation at trial that he had forgotten about it. Under oath, that was his testimony. He couldn't remember the number.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He couldn't remember a lot of things at that December interview that he should have remembered and, of course, from my perspective that was an indication that certainly at that December 1999 interview he was being very untruthful with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Okay. I'll move on to something else. And in this area, let's go to a chapter of our discussion. I want to go over your participation in the questioning process of witnesses. As I recall, you testified back on -- it was the first day, November 10th, 2003. You were asked about an -- it's on page 4.237. You were asked if you were present during the interviews. And you gave a particular answer. If you could look at that. And if you find it, it should be 4.237, and I believe it goes on to 4.238. You were asked on line -- I believe it starts with line 13: "At the time of the investigation did you sit in on any interviews of witnesses?" And your answer was: "I sat in during investigation in numerous interviews, and on those interviews where I was not able to go because of other commitments, I read the interviews after they were finished. So I have access to all of that information." The next question: "Why were you actually present during interviews of various people?" And this is the aspect that I'm going to be focusing on, answer, line 20: "Well, certainly during the early days of the investigation and the initial interviews that we started conducting in 1998, as the military analyst, logically I was the person who had the broadest background as to the military context of the individual and the questions that would be asked. Most of these interviews were, in fact, of VRS military officers. So it was pretty much, you know, a logical conclusion that I would be the person in there to be able to assist investigators and the lawyers who were present as a component of preparing for and in the interview to determine not how accurate the individual is speaking, but to ensure that on follow-on questions, we can get complete answers with respect to military issues." Do you recall being asked those questions and giving those answers?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, from reading your answer, it would appear to me that you were there as an asset for the investigators and the Prosecutors, because you had the military background. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's inappropriate for the lawyer to interject his own personal viewpoint in the questions. That is something that is not ever relevant and is not necessary. The question can be phrased in the same exact way, but it's not appropriate for it to be made personal like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey, I think the testimony of that witness during that trial is quite clear. There's proper foundation for the lawyer to ask this question. But on the other hand, Mr. Karnavas, I hope you sometimes just read the transcript word by word.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, were you there strictly to provide assistance to Prosecutors, like Peter McCloskey who was there, asking questions of witnesses?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I provided assistance before and during the interviews, and in some instances I actually asked questions of the interviewees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your function at the time? Investigator? Interrogator? Analyst? What was it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Analyst.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you weren't there to investigate?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not a credentialed investigator, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That wasn't my question. My question was: Were you there to investigate? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, analysis is a function of investigation. I mean --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what is the answer then?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there as part of the investigative process. And in that, I analysed, and as part of my questioning, I assume that that will qualify as investigate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So you were there to investigate as well as analyse?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the two can be split apart, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, your role as a questioner, was that strictly related to military aspects or would you jump in on occasion to ask questions that you thought might be relevant in other aspects of the investigative case?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be fair, Mr. Karnavas, there have been a lot of those. My general practice was that I would interject if there was a military-related follow-on question or a contextual one. However, I certainly won't rule out the possibility that I may have interjected as to another aspect of the case. If you have specifics that would be helpful, but it's been a lot of years and a lot of interviews, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there have been cases where -- instances I should say, instances where you were quite active in asking the questions?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are -- have been one or two interviews where I was quite active, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, again, I just want to make sure I understand it, were you trying to focus on the military aspects, getting -- trying to get information from the witnesses, so then you could as an independent, objective analyst, and not as an investigator for the Prosecution team, get information to analyse it and provide us with an objective viewpoint. What was it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I'm not independent, per se. I work for and am a member of the Office of the Prosecutor and I am integrated into the investigative team. The reports that I write and the conclusions that I try to make, I believe are as fair and balanced as possible. But I'm not going to sit up here and say that I'm an independent outsider, obviously I'm not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be almost impossible for me, considering that we're talking about a military-related war crime issue, for me, on one hand, to say that I could focus strictly on the military analytical aspects or dissecting the Drina Corps, and on the other hand not have to deal with some of the criminal-related linkage that ties back to the military. It's an impossible and strictly artificial difference.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But I guess my question is -- goes more towards your intense association with that particular team as you travelled around acting as an investigator as well as an analyst, to what extent that might have affected your objectivity as an analyst. That's -- do you think that that might have in some way skewed your objectivity?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I like to think that it does not; however, I am human. It may very well have had an impact on some aspects of it. I try very hard as a component of my report, over 670 footnote citations, as a way of trying to prevent that. Also as part of the process, I have access to a number of other military analysts who work on different cases and different issues, and I am very active with them in discussing a lot of these issues looking for alternative points of view, strictly as an exercise to prevent any form of bias from creeping into my analysis. So while I cannot say I'm perfect, I try to take and I actively work to take steps to reduce bias, even though it exists.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And all those people, by the way, that you consult, they're like you working for the Prosecution, non-independent, members of their team working to solve cases that the Prosecutors for whom they work with and for are interested in achieving a result of guilt?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are certainly not independent as the analysts. We work to solve cases for the Prosecutor, that's correct. We're -- certainly the analysts are less concerned with the issue of achieving innocence and guilt and are more concerned with the issue of being as factually and contextually accurate as possible. As I indicated yesterday, that is -- as analysts, we believe that is what the Office of the Prosecutor wants from us. We try to do that as much as we possibly can. And where the contextual facts lay out, whether they prove innocence or guilt is an issue we tend to leave for the Court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, just for the record, I just want to touch on a couple of interviews, portions of interviews, where you've interjected yourself. And maybe you could tell us what was the purpose behind those questions or whatever they -- the sections refer to. So I'm going to -- I would like to show you a transcript that has been marked -- will be marked for identification purposes as D81/1. And if you could get it handy.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have me at a disadvantage, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Okay. If we could --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we get a copy. This is the first time we've heard of anything along these lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I thought that we distributed sufficient copies, but obviously ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If you could just look at the front page first of all, and it notes that this was an interview taken on 1st December 2001. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then it designates the individual's name. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if you flip to page -- well, that's the problem. These are not paginated, but I guess we did it by hand. Page 66. This is how we received them, though there may be an updated version of them.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And there it clearly denotes, does it not, that you are going on record. Towards the bottom of the page, at the end of the page it says: "Richard Butler: Okay, for the record my name is Richard Butler." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you said that you have a couple of questions pertaining to going over some of the information you've already given the investigators and the team this morning. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you go to the next page towards the middle of it, you ask a question, and I'll read it and follow along -- it's page 67 --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to put this on the ELMO because I'm not sure of the status of the individual.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I think everybody has copies and that's why I agree. You indicate --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just a matter of procedure, I think the procedure has been established that there should be a question. If there's a document or something where he can be impeached, he can be impeached. If there's a document to refresh his recollection. But this merely just reading out things for comment is really not an appropriate part of common law adversarial procedure. And it could go on forever. And if it just -- that's why the witness is here. Just reading transcripts forever, you know, is just not proper.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I would like to respond to that. First, it's a technique that I see quite often used by the Prosecution in the Milosevic case. So it is used. Secondly, we are not in the common law jurisdiction. Thirdly, even if we were in one, it would be permitted for me to read and then discuss, because obviously I have to get the gentleman to read it and we have to get it on the record, especially in light of the Court's ruling that all these documents don't come in. Thirdly, the gentleman indicated that he was there. He stated his position of what he was doing and how he was doing it. I'm now going to point to -- not to every question, because we do have a list of 19 individuals that he's questioned. We've even broken it down. I'm going to go through two witnesses to give the Court an impression of the gentleman's participation and how he was questioning people. So I think it's relevant to the issue. It goes to the issue of bias. I'm not saying that the man is biased, but it's just something that will need to be considered by the Court. And lastly, I would like to say that last week I exercised an enormous amount of restraint, even though I should have been objecting because of the Court's ruling. Now I feel I'm being sabotaged by the Prosecution jumping up and down and objecting for no reason. So I would like to have some consistency. This is proper. We've done it before and I don't intend to read large portions, but I think the gentleman should be given an opportunity to comment for the record. And again, at some point, I will be arguing at the close of this trial that perhaps his testimony and his reports should be viewed with a pinch of salt. That's all. This goes to his character for bias and it was an issue that was raised by the Prosecution on direct. They asked the question: Were you there? When they asked the question, and that's why I read it into the record again to refresh his memory, it would appear that he was just sitting there providing some mere guidance, perhaps with the occasional question. I'm trying to show that is not true, accurate, and complete. They opened the door. I'm merely trying to close it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I quite understand your objections and the -- as for the point you are going to make, I think it's the conclusion that the Bench should draw on whether this witness is biased or not. Of course you could show your case to the Bench. And here we are talking about a procedural matter. I think since everybody has got this document and we could read it by ourselves, and if you have questions, just ask the question. And if a certain part is particularly important to your case, you may read it out for the record. But do not read so many paragraphs, the whole page. I hope you could put your question up to the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I can, Your Honour. And, see, I'm trying to readjust to your earlier reading. If we could have, for instance, a modified ruling from your -- from the initial ruling that we had from the Bench, in that I would at least be able to introduce the pages from which the testimony was taken as opposed to the entire document, fine. Otherwise, if I just ask the question, these documents don't go into the record, there is no record then from which the Court can discern. It becomes very difficult. And so that's why if I can have it as an exhibit, just the relevant portions that are asked, then I don't need to read. So I'm trying to abide by the Court's ruling and at the same time make my record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you could, but try to reduce the parts to as little as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm trying, Your Honour. It's not easy sometimes. Very well. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we could go to page 67 and just -- here you ask a question and I just want to read the relevant -- the question itself. You say: "I have to tell you, considering the events that were occurring, and they were of such magnitude and size that everyone," and I underscore you say, "everyone in Bratunac was aware of what was going on. I find it difficult to believe that a captain assigned to the logistics branch of the Bratunac Brigade, at a time when the brigade was fully mobilised and when people's work obligations were being called and then they were being mobilised, would be spending his days picking raspberries." Now, my question to you is what was the purpose of telling him that everybody knew in Bratunac? Was that -- just if you could answer that question.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, Mr. Karnavas, in the context of what we were talking about, everyone in Bratunac knew that Srebrenica had fallen and that there were tens of thousands of Bosnian Muslims in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I guess the form of the question, are you there trying to get information or are you there trying to browbeat him like an interrogator, you know -- and as I understand it, the military does have professional interrogators, within the context of your particular field, which is intelligence?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir they do, and no, sir, I am not one of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And I'm not suggesting that you are. But would you not agree with me that there in that particular question, you're trying to somehow intimidate the individual?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I believe that if you go to the previous question and put the two in context, I'm making it clear that given his prior statement to the investigator and one of my other analysts, that I do not believe that he has associated himself with the entire time of picking raspberries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So that was a conclusion that you had reached at that time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the information that was told to me by the investigator and the analyst who sat in at the first part of that interview, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they had information that he had not been out picking raspberries?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information that we had was that he was a rostered member of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given the circumstances that were occurring at the time, we found - and in my opinion, I found - an argument that he was, in fact, not performing any military duty and picking raspberries as somewhere beyond credibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But at the same time you've already indicated to us that one of the tasks for the military police was to go around rounding up people that were leaving their posts when they were supposed to be serving their duty. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct but it does not normally apply to captains in the logistics branch. Officers have a less frequent instance of going absent without official leave than do conscripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a reservist or an academy graduate?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a reservist like almost all the other Bratunac Brigade officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would he have been in that position if he was in the JNA, because -- and I mention this only because we're going to be getting to it, but you seem to be implying that they more or less wholesale adopted the JNA doctrine and by virtue of doing so implemented it accordingly.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've lost your question on which issue we're talking about --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm going to object to relevance, whether this guy is the kind of officer that might be out picking raspberries, I don't see the relevance any further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, we don't see the relevance here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I do want to put the Court on notice, I will be objecting, in spite the Court's instructions, if it's allowed for the Prosecution to just object whenever they wish. I think their objections are designed only to obstruct, and I say this with all due candour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karnavas. I think the Bench would decide what kind of nature the objection is. It's not your responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now -- so it's your conclusion, you had concluded on the spot that this reservist, captain, could not have been out picking raspberries?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that my conclusion was that I found it difficult to believe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you ask him where he was picking raspberries?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to go back and look at the entire remainder of the interview to know the specific questions, and there are another 24 pages, I believe, 23 pages, so it would take a while. I don't know exactly what questions I asked him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether it was raspberry season?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am informed it was raspberry season, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were these not also -- were these not also citizen soldiers, including these reservist officers, serving in and around the areas where they lived?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And were these not also hard times for these people that were living there during these war conditions?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that they were difficult times for them, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And isn't it a fact in that region if you go to it, one of the staples is the agricultural -- the agriculture. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if you could go to page 80. Again, the top of the page. Again, just a vignette here. We're not going to go through the entire interview. "Do you know" - here is you making a statement, it would appear - "Do you know that in late September and in early October, the forces of the Bratunac Brigade, some of them from the rear services branch, no doubt some of them from the engineering equipment in Vihor dug up the mass graves in Glogova at night, after night and transferred the trucks to graves in Zeleni Jadar. And every night trucks filled with decomposing bodies were passed through the town where everyone could smell it?" Now, my question is: Here you say, I want to highlight, "no doubt". Again, you seem to be injecting your opinion into the question, no?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we -- was this a military question? Did this have to do with military?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, looking in the context, as a logistics officer, which he was, and the inference that the rear services branches would have been involved in that in a similar manner that they were in Zvornik, I consider this to be a military question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And a question one that the Prosecutor who was there would have been incapable of formulating or conceiving in their mind, and therefore a military analyst of your expertise was necessary at the time?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. That's argumentative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It goes to what he indicated on direct. He was only there as support.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that this is a little bit more than support? More like intimidation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to whether or not the investigator or other analysts who were involved in the beginning of the interview had already asked that question, I don't know. But my goal behind that question was that we had already received from a number of individuals the issue that there was a general awareness within the town of Bratunac about the reburial operation. A number of witnesses had indicated that at night they could smell the bodies going by, and that as a member of the rear services of the Bratunac Brigade, that the issue that he had no awareness of this, again, I didn't think was credible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, but my question is: Why was it necessary for Analyst Butler to ask the question and not the investigator or whoever was involved?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that he didn't ask the question earlier. I asked the question because, again as I noted, he indicated that the rear services company, to his knowledge, did not have any activity with respect to that. And I believe that the information that we have indicates that there were at least some elements that would have been involved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you had already formed a conclusion and now you're trying to verify this conclusion. And when you were getting nowhere, you were giving him information, letting him know that everybody knew, more or less trying to break him down and sort of give you what you thought the information that he had?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was asked the question from a point of view that trying to get a truthful answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Thank you. If we could go to just one more interview. And this is a short one. I think one reference only, one vignette. What has been marked D80/1 for identification purposes. If you could look at it and as we can see, this is dated 2nd December 2001. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And in fact it's the first page also notes the gentleman's name that is being interviewed?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. And I would appreciate if you would not mention that name. I know that this individual has had some problems. I'm just raising the issue now. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your guidance. And it would appear that he's being interviewed in Banja Luka. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just from the first page, I just want to point out that we see your name?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it from your earlier answer or your earlier remark, you have a vivid recollection of this particular interview or interviewing the individual?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we could -- let me have one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I need one moment to find the page, Your Honour. I have an unpaginated version. I don't know how ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, we could have an early break, and during the break you could try to organise your documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I would appreciate that. And I truly apologise for taking up the Court's time in this fashion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll resume until 5 minutes to 4.00

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. You found that page?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. And I apologise again, Your Honour. If I could direct everyone's attention to page 34 to what has been marked for identification purposes as D80.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you found it, Mr. Butler?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: 34, yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it starts with your name, does it not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to read and then we're going to have to have a little discussion. You state here: "I understand your position and I understand the threat that you are under. I understand your decision. And hopefully in time, as the situation changes and as you see the situation change you can again come forward with information that we can use to prosecute the guilty and keep the innocent from being caught up in that process. Everyone knows what happened in Eastern Bosnia in July of 1995. You are a military officer. You know what it takes to move thousands of people from one location to another. You know how many soldiers are needed to guard these people. You know how many bulldozers and engineers that are required to bury the bodies. It's not anything that happened by magic. You know this. The officers of the Drina Corps know this. The officers of the Zvornik Brigade, the Bratunac Brigade, the protection battalion of the 65th Battalion Regiment, Milici, Vlasenica, everyone knows this, and everyone knows that at the end of the day, there are very few people who are responsible for doing this, that a lot of people had parts in it, whether by choice or whether they are forced to. We are not looking for people who are forced to leave -- we are not looking for people who were forced to have a role. Drazen Erdemovic was forced to shoot people at Branjevo Form. His friends later put a bullet in him, but he told of his role there. He doesn't go away from life. In many ways, he's seen as a victim, just as the victim who he shot. There are a lot of awful -- there are an awful lot of Drazen Erdemovics who were forced to do things; the difference is that Drazen Erdemovic is now living a new life somewhere. And the hundreds who were forced to do things are not and will not. And we'll just leave it at that." Now, where is the question in this portion that I read?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There isn't one in that portion, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I thought you were there, based on your testimony --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could we have the microphone for the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My apologies. Can you ask the question again, sir, I don't think they caught it for the record.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. My question was: Where is the question in the statement?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer was: There is no question there, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And as I understand your testimony earlier was you were there to assist the Prosecutors and the investigators in the event they needed, you know, some military expertise that they could rely on you to provide them with that information in order to ask the proper questions. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And yet here we see no question, do we?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in that particular passage that you just read, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, you're not only making a statement, but you're drawing some conclusions, are you not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this respect, yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. For instance, you're telling him: "Everyone knows what happened in Eastern Bosnia in July of 1995." Right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that's a conclusion that you had reached that everyone, and I take it you're speaking everyone in what, all Serbs, everyone in Bosnia and Herzegovina, or everyone in the world? Which one is it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I think I'll keep that one limited to everyone in Eastern Podrinje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And that was, I take it, a conclusion that you had reached at that time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have failed to meet anyone yet who had not heard of Srebrenica and wasn't aware of the background and the events that occurred. So I didn't I was reaching very far on that one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So I guess this is only limited to what that they had heard that something had happened, not to the events, the actual details of the events. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you go on further down and then you say, you know this the officers, you say the Drina Corps, the Zvornik Brigade, Bratunac Brigade, Protection Battalion of the 65th Milici and so on and so forth. And you say: "Everyone knows at the end of the day that there were very few people who were responsible." Now, was this your opinion at this time that all these folks knew about what was going on and knew of all the details?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular case and before I get into the context behind this particular passage, I prefer to do it in private session, given the sensitivities involved. In this particular respect, I was trying to, with this particular individual who had received and to my knowledge as recently six months ago, continues to receive threats, this was one of the issues -- one of the issues was that he was very fearful about saying anything or cooperating or even talking with the Office of the Prosecutor. As I say, I can go into more the context of the details of this, but I prefer to do that in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Can we go into private session, Your Honour, for this answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, is it necessary to go into the very details of this issue? I don't think that the answer of this witness is contrary to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. I stand corrected. You're absolutely right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It would appear here during some sort of -- they're using some psychology to motivate this person to come forward and also you're using the name of Drazen Erdemovic as a good example. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would -- I don't know if I'm using psychology, but certainly in this particular instance I used Drazen Erdemovic as an individual who came forward and testified as to his role in the massacres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you're also explaining your conclusion, you're telling this individual that everybody knows everything, basically, from all of these brigades in the corps. Isn't that the purpose of it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I believe that in this respect, most of the local population knows a great deal about the individuals who or who were not involved. And as I indicated in that passage that you read, one of the goals that we have is to not catch people up in the investigative process who have no role. And as I expect you know from travelling and being in Bratunac, any mere association with the Office of the Prosecutor in that respect carries with it a significant threat for reprisal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you tell him that basically Erdemovic, who got approximately a month for each innocent life that he took as a reward for coming forward is, in your eyes, a victim, just like the victims that he took -- he snuffed lives of. Right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular context where Drazen Erdemovic is a low-ranking soldier whom - and he'll testify to this, so I'm not going to put words in his mouth, I presume - was put in a position where if he did not execute individuals, he himself would be killed, he may very well be a victim. That is an unfortunate lot in life for being a soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is an individual who said, okay, then he executed over a hundred and then supposedly found the courage to tell the same person who had told him, "take the line if you don't execute," "I throw my hands up, I'm through executing for the day," correct, and I'm paraphrasing, but that is in essence his testimony?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is, in essence, I believe. And again, that's a morality judgement on his part, not mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, it took over a hundred lives for him to take -- before he decided that he had enough and, in fact, nothing happened to him?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that he was shot a week later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Bijeljina, over other matters.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that it was unrelated, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Okay, well. Just a couple of questions on this. Were you acting as Butler the analyst here, the military analyst here or was it Butler the interrogator, or Butler the investigator, or what was your role and function at this juncture at this interview?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in this specific interview, this is actually rather a completely different role for me. As you will note in the context of the entire interview, the individual when he came forward and started discussing his military background, it became very clear to me because of my association with other military analysts on other cases, that his background would make him an important witness with respect to at least two and perhaps three other cases. Obviously, Mr. Bursik the investigator was with me the whole time. Clearly Mr. Bursik, focussing on Srebrenica, does not know a lot of the contextual issues behind those other investigations. In that respect, I played a leading role in this interview, not only to elicit the information with respect to those that would be of use to those other investigations, but also the fact that the individual I was talking to was a professional military officer who was very fearful for certain circumstances with his family. So like I said, this is rather an anomaly as to how active I am in an interview. However, under the circumstances I think I conducted myself appropriately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, were you there -- were you not there to interview a witness for Srebrenica? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was summonsed for his role in Srebrenica, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And so this conversation and this interview has nothing to do with other cases that you claim today, but rather the focus of the interview was his knowledge and/or possible involvement in Srebrenica. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think if you read the first 17 pages of the interview, you'll find out that that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The passage that I read has nothing to do with trying to elicit information from someone; instead it's you imparting information. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And one of the things you were trying to do in your role -- as your role, I guess, as an analyst, was to flip, to use a common term, to flip a witness; in other words, make him your own. Correct? Not that there's anything wrong with that, but that's what you were trying to do?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that that would be the phraseology of what I was doing, however very clearly what I was attempting to do is to make the individual understand that within the context of what the investigation was looking for, that his information was of value, even though I agree with his perception that he wasn't there at the commission of the crimes and had left the area before. What we were looking for in this context was that because he had ties to that city, the information we were trying to elicit from him was with respect to what information he had heard as well as what information he knew people weren't involved in these things. So in this respect, it wasn't firsthand information; what it was, we were looking for information that he might be able to use to give us further investigative leads.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the bottom line after that long-winded explanation is you wanted to make him your own witness?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wanted to certainly get him to cooperate with the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he would become a cooperating witness?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And I take it at that point he wasn't cooperating enough to provide you the sort of information or to go into the details that you and the others wanted him to provide you. Right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. Like I said, in the greater context, there's more to the story with respect to beyond this interview. And that's what I don't want to get into in public session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one last question. Was the investigator that was with you there at the time Mr. Bursik, isn't he a trained investigator?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, he is. And he's a fine one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there's nothing in the statement that you made that he could not make, since he was there to investigate and you were there to provide backup military analytical information to the Prosecution team. Right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I disagree. And if you would go back to the beginning of the statement, most of the information discussed in the first 18 pages were areas that are well beyond the scope of the investigation that he's involved in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, my question was right to that statement that you made. So don't go off the reservation. Stay with me on this statement, on this particular statement, the one that you made, the one where you're trying to flip him over and make him a cooperating Prosecution witness. That statement could have been made by the investigator and not by the analyst. It has nothing to do with military information that someone of your calibre need to have. Right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I trust that Mr. Bursik could have made that statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, before we leave the issue of statements, questioning statements, were you present when General Zivanovic was interviewed by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I was not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that would have been back on July 2nd, 2001.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That you were not or --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I was not present, but your day is correct, I believe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My day is correct but at one point your name pops up, that's why?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's unsurprising --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's unsurprising or surprising?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: My name tends to pop up frequently in a number of interviews with VRS officers concerning this. My public testimony has gotten around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Well, were you aware, since we're on the gentleman, were you aware that he had indicated to Peter McCloskey, who was there as part of the team, to interview -- he had suggested that he should interview Colonel Blagojevic. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have been aware -- when I first read the statement it would have been approximately the first week of August is when it was transcribed. That particular comment that we should interview Colonel Blagojevic doesn't ring a bell. I trust it's there, but it just doesn't ring a bell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this, since you were part of this military analytical team trying to piece all the pieces together, at least in this particular case Nikolic was interviewed, Obrenovic was interviewed, Mr. Jokic was interviewed, and yet OTP and you, as part of that team, never made any efforts to interview Colonel Blagojevic. Is there particular reason?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is a misstatement of the facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It is not a misstatement of the facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't think counsel wants to go into that situation. We would love to talk to your client and this is --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He never --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Do not talk to each other. Do not talk to each other. I think we have to cool down. I understand that there is some disputes on this issue. And I give the floor to Mr. McCloskey first.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think what Mr. Karnavas means to be getting at is, if he can tie it to a time frame, he may be okay. But these general comments that the Prosecution has never been interested in Blagojevic is more what my objection is about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I will be more than happy to give them a time frame. Before -- let me back up, let me lay a little foundation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before Mr. Nikolic was arrested, he was interviewed, was he not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was invited. He came. You interviewed him. Off he went. And then at some later point he was arrested. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if my memory serves me correct, he was supposed to come back again to be interviewed as a suspect. The first time was only as a witness and then he had -- he was unavailable. Are you aware of that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. There's no foundation for that statement and I don't believe that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm asking the gentleman; he can verify it, yea or nay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, this man has to have a factual basis for his questions, he can't just go on a fishing on facts that especially affect people that are about to be sentenced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well. Well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll go on to the next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you interested in interviewing Nikolic again, before he was arrested; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the investigation was interested in interviewing him again, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether he was ever invited back or whether he was ever invited or being tracked down to be invited to come back, to give a second interview, this time as a suspect and not as a witness, as he was interviewed the first time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe he was tracked down, summonsed through the Republika Srpska, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And that was before or after his arrest?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was before, I believe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And did he show up for that summons?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the second interview?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that -- well, I don't know -- I believe he showed up for the second one as a suspect. I'm not sure. I don't know all the mechanics about that, because I was working a separate case at the time. So I'll trust that he did if that's the presumption that you make. I don't know the details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't have a second interview statement, so I can only presume, using your analytical techniques, that he didn't show up?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if he was summonsed again or not. I would have to check with the investigation on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Colonel Obrenovic was summoned, was he not, to give a statement?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was summonsed, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he showed up?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: After one delay, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he showed up?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he gave a statement?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it one or two statements that he gave?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe he gave us a total of two statements, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And then the other gentleman involved in this case, Major Jokic, he was summoned as well, was he not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he came?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Colonel Blagojevic was never summoned, was he?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, he was not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was just arrested?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That is a misstatement of the facts. It's --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I would like to know what the facts are, Your Honour. What are the facts? He was never summoned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let us hear. The witness is going to tell us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was never summoned, was he?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If he was not summoned, he cannot come forward to give a statement, can he?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, the answer is actually fairly straightforward on this one. At the same time that General Krstic was indicted, Colonel Blagojevic was indicted and Colonel Pandurevic was indicted.
