At that time, and I believe it continues, it is the policy of the Office of the Prosecutor not to attempt to summons or interview people who are indicted and who are wanted. Further, at that time, despite the fact that we now know that Colonel Blagojevic was in Banja Luka pretty much in plain sight, the Office of the Prosecutor with respect to apprehension and SFOR, to my knowledge, were not aware of that or did not put the pieces together. And certainly we didn't put them together in the OTP. And I don't know when SFOR put them together to locate Colonel Blagojevic. But that is the short answer to the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the short answer also is that you indicted the man without giving him the courtesy of an invitation to be questioned by someone like you present, the military analyst, who was looking for as much information in order to present an unbiased report. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, just to clarify that, I didn't indict anybody --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't say that you did.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says on the thing. In that respect, neither was General Krstic and neither was Colonel Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, what's your level of education?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I am a college graduate. Thank you for asking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask -- did you hear my question --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- And were you able to understand it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you allow me to continue, I can explain it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't need an explanation, I need a direct answer from you. Okay? So could you please --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is completely argumentive. I know it's night court and that tempers get frayed, but this is not helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I am demonstrating the witness is being flip with the Court. He may think that he's the star here but he needs to answer the questions directly. He knows how to, there's no cultural divide here, Your Honour; we're from the same culture and he understands me and I understand him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, first of all I believe that this question is one of the most direct to the witness. He answered your question with a very short answer, yes or no or correct, which is much to our satisfaction. Secondly, we do not see your point. In most of jurisdictions, if you arrest or indict somebody, do you have to give the courtesy to have an interview with that person? I don't think so, so I fail to see your point in your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The point is, Your Honour, before they indicted him, they made a decision that he was guilty, that's why they indicted him. They could have given him the opportunity, like they gave others, to give a statement. They chose not to. It goes to the bias how they have already fixed in the targets, they made up their mind and they are proceeding in a fashion how they are going to somehow get to their result, irrespective of what the evidence may be. That is my point, Your Honour. Before he was indicted if they thought he was a suspect, they could have interviewed him. They chose not to. And this is the military analyst.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, this is your argument. I quite understand your argument. But as the general practice of every jurisdiction, I cannot completely agree with your argument at this point. But this is another matter. And I understand your point. I understand your point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Shall we move on?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We'll move on. That was my last point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I can have one second, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's talk about zones of responsibility, something that's more pleasant, perhaps more familiar. Now, in looking at your -- the two volumes or the two reports that you presented, the narratives, you tend to use at times zone of operation --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly give the interpreters a few moments to catch up, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I guess I'll proceed at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't hear another voice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I notice that in your narratives, you sort of use sometimes area, zone of operation, zone of responsibility, and first, I guess, I wanted to talk about that. When you used those terms, are you exact each and every time in your narratives? In other words, do you mean one thing when you say "area of responsibility" or "zone of responsibility" or "zone of operation"? Do they all mean the same thing?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular respect when I use the phrase "area of responsibility" or "zone of responsibility," that means the same thing. And area of operations is -- I differentiate. So an area of operations is something more specific than a zone of responsibility or an area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So -- all right. Now, as I understand it, as I understand your testimony, is it your opinion that the brigades have a zone of responsibility. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And I take it that is an opinion that has been formed by you based on your study of the rules and regulations as they existed at the time of July 1995. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is based on the documents as well as the general formulation of interviews that we've had with various individuals within the structure of the VRS. So that's what I base this on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the individuals that you questioned, were they all suspects, witnesses, folks that you were trying to track down, or were they independent, you know, someone who is outside of the Srebrenica question and you were trying to get them to help you out on the application and interpretation of the rules?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The individuals in question were those people who were summonsed as witnesses or suspects with respect to team 6. I understand that to broaden the context out, I've also had access to the interviews of individuals that are VRS officers in other geographic regions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wanted for other or being questioned for other --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are being questioned in connection with other activities, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me rephrase it a little bit. Did you ever go outside to get an independent analyst, someone with, say, your like background, from the former Yugoslavia, be it from whatever nation or nationality, to help you interpret these rules?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe that we did that, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the question was not to "we" but it was to you. Did you -- no, no. Please let me ask the question, because we is -- we is a lot. I'm asking you, Mr. Butler. Did Mr. Butler as the military analyst that was preparing this narrative for Srebrenica, did he, in his official capacity or even unofficial capacity, meet with someone from the former Yugoslavia who might be an expert on the JNA in order to go through, read, and analyse the rules?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So basically, you had the rules, which obviously we can all read, you had your own background as a military analyst of, you know, analysing other armies and other places, such as in the Warsaw, for instance, the Warsaw Pact, those armies. And then, of course, we have the documents in this case. And then you were getting information from officers who were being called by the Office of the Prosecution to give information about Srebrenica. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that some of those officers, if not all of them, might have had a slight anxiety when they received the invitation to meet with the Office of the Prosecution to be questioned officially about an event which the whole world has characterised as a monumental atrocity?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I take it that may well have been the case in some instances.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it that one can conclude that perhaps not knowing, even though they may have been characterised as a witness or a suspect, they wouldn't necessarily know whether one day they would be in the dock themselves. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suspect in some cases that may be correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would it also be correct that some of those people from whom you were trying to get information in order to understand and learn the mechanics of the VRS may have had reasons, for instance, to minimise their roles?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to the --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With respect to anything.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't want to leave it that broad. With respect to noncriminal activities, in many cases they were particularly willing to discuss those issues.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you feel sufficiently confident that all of those individuals were providing you accurate information with respect to the application of the rules?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the particular respect to the applicability of the rules of the former JNA, I'm comfortable with what the witnesses have said is an accurate and relatively complete description of that. And I believe that it, in fact, was relatively well confirmed, even by the Defence witness in the Krstic case who -- the Defence expert in the Krstic case who also acknowledged that those were the regulations in play. So I believe I'm on a firm foundation here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm not asking whether the regulations were in place. I think there we can pretty much agree on. There's another opportunity where we agree. But I'm saying how these regulations were interpreted and applied in the field in Bosnia and Herzegovina or in this area in 1995. That's what I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I mean, clearly there were going to be deviations from those regulations as they were applied 12 to 13 years later, and that is why I look at the documents as valuable, as being able to follow those deviations where essentially the lessons from combat are learned and applied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But my question again -- I just want to nail this point down before we go any further, and it's not a trick question. In interviewing these witnesses and suspects that had been summoned by OTP to give evidence regarding Srebrenica, who by your own admission had something to be nervous about, not knowing whether one day they would be indicted, were you sufficiently confident that the information they would give you on the applicability of the rules was correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, not initially, but through time I became very confident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, in general is not true that superior military commanders use various control measures in order to make the most effective use of the subordinate units in combat operations?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a general principle or are we focusing on the former JNA rules?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're focusing in general. We're going to go from the very general.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's fair, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you say that applied to the JNA?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that would apply to the VRS as well?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those principles were applicable in the VRS as well, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, there are some principles, in fact, that more or less all organised armies apply. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. There are some that are known as universal principles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the army is a fairly structured organisation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because that's the only way it can function. Right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Effectively, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so that's why you have rules and regulations so that those who are in the business of implementing those rules and regulations know exactly what it is that they need to implement and how to implement?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Essentially it defines the scope of their confidence and the means by which they implement them, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very loosely, and I know there is a whole philosophy and a whole science behind that, very loosely when you wrap up all of that, it's considered doctrine, military doctrine. I don't need the whole academic spiel, I'm just saying loosely, but go ahead.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: A doctrine is a broader philosophy. And in the context of the former JNA a doctrine would be All People's Defence. In this particular instance what we're talking about is the regulatory basis by which that is followed. Doctrine and regulations are not interchangeable terms. The regulatory basis exists to allow the doctrine to be implemented. Sometimes those terms get mixed up so I just want to clarify.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "All People's Defence," that would be what you would consider the doctrine for the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And I take it that would apply to Bosnia and Herzegovina at this particular time frame?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- well, for -- I assume for 1995 with respect to the VRS, they were implementing the JNA basis of the regulations. Whether or not on a broader level they were encompassing all the principles of All People's Defence, I don't know. But certainly where they could use it in the conduct of their military campaigns and in the content -- conduct of their general military strategy, they did so. It was all they had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it you're familiar with the All People's Defence?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At a very broad level. Not at the specific, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know of its applicability prior to the war in 1992?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in detail, sir. No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I guess we'll skip that part of the discussion. Now, getting back to my initial question, don't such control measures constrain the geographical positions of the subordinate units, that is the control measures that are put in place?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They generally define the boundaries and limits or axes of advance of subordinate units. Again it depends on what echelon we're talking about, but yes, as a general rule, the superior formation defines the area of operations or the axis of advance or the limits of boundaries for subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, and so that would apply to the VRS at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And these control measures, just to name a few, would they not include the sectors, various zones, face lines, limits of advance?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you're mixing terminology in some cases. I think the control measures itself are orders and directives which lay out the various boundaries and borders. So maybe the terminology is my mistake on this one. I consider a control measure is the actual order that delineates what those are. Those actual borders and definitions themselves are what's found in them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I wasn't referring to one particular order. But I'm saying when they're trying to -- I mean, you have so many resources at your disposal and now I would assume one of the responsibilities of a commander is to determine how to best use those resources, you know, given the situation that's occurring at any given moment. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in this particular case, we know that the VRS, the Main Staff, had at some point established the Drina Corps. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that did not exist prior to 1992, that particular corps?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Drina Corps was formed in November 1992. It did not exist as a former JNA function or it did not exist from a JNA unit prior to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So for a period of time, the -- that area had territorial defences, the TOs, providing some of the security measures for their residents. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. For the most part the units that were formed or the units that were existing in 1992 and which were brought into the Drina Corps had their basis in former TO units that were essentially based or supported by their parent municipalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So there was no -- all right. Now -- and the TOs, the Territorial Defence, that was part of the All People's Defence, was it not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence was a part of that. I mean, it was a two-tiered structure. It was the JNA as the active force --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The military.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military and the TO, or the Territorial Defence, as the force that would be mobilised on the basis of conflict to assist and take part in the activity with the JNA depending on the external threat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And one was located outside the cities and one was for the cities?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure how it works Bosnia-wide, but with respect to just the Drina Corps, my analysis indicates that they were generally based on a municipal level is how they were organised from the May/June 1992 time frame.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it would be fair to say that JNA, for instance, they would be the professional military, and then the Territorial Defence would be more homegrown?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that the JNA was the professional military and that the Territorial Defence, in fact, was the individuals who had served their active duty allocations. And under the doctrine of All People's Defence you were in the reserves until 65, those were where many of those people were. A lot of them also served in the JNA when they came off reserve duty. So it is two complementary branches of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And I take it the TOs did have some professional staff at the top, you know, with the commander of the local TO or was he a reservist as well?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, my limited understanding of the circumstances as it existed Bosnia-wide, I know that in Eastern Bosnia there were, in fact, JNA officers, and I believe it was a common practice that JNA active duty officers would serve rotations in the TO in many of the positions of leadership, not only on the TO staff but in some of the units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I take it those serving in the JNA that were holding certain positions had to be trained military officers, as opposed to just nontrained?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. They were professionally and educated military officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it there were some guidelines that designated at what particular rank somebody would hold a particular position?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they changed over times through the late 1980s as the country started to fall apart in the civil war, to my knowledge until the JNA essentially disbanded, they tried as much as they could to maintain the qualities of professionalism in its officer ranks over who was in command and at what position. So they did try to adhere to that as much as possible under the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And I take it the advancement process was pretty regimented as well, was it not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my understanding, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I believe you have indicated that the doctrine from the JNA was more or less transferred over or absorbed by or taken over, whatever word you choose, by the VRS?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, not necessarily the broader doctrine, but the combat regulations, the regulatory basis of the JNA was adopted for the most part by the VRS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But as I understand your testimony correctly, and we'll get into it a little bit more in detail, it's my understanding that it is your opinion that the VRS more or less worked or operated like the JNA. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. What I said was, and as a component of my testimony, it was that the VRS adopted the regulations of the former JNA. I did not ever say that it worked more or less like the JNA. The VRS only equates to the JNA with respect to a nucleus of professional officers and that they're following the same operating regulations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And is it your testimony that they were indeed following the operating regulations, the methodologies that go with it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As much as they -- as much as it was practical under the circumstances, and I believe it was very much as much as they could. There were very few deviations that I could determine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's where I want to pin you down a little bit, if you don't mind, because I want to know, I want to be certain. Are you saying there was some deviations, in other words by and large, for the most part, not only had they adopted but they were also applying these methodologies? Is that what you're trying to tell us?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to the combat regulations, the organisation of formations, the methodologies used in the command and staff process, the VRS, not only did they adopt the ones of the former JNA, but as the JNA dissolved in May of 1992, the VJ was formed. As the VJ modified some of those the VRS tried to remain in step as much as possible with that as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously, given the circumstances on the ground at the time, there was not going to be full compliance on all issues. But as a general rule, they followed the former JNA methodologies as much as practicable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So I take it if we were to go into the regulations that they were applying and that they had taken over from the JNA, we would be able to find, for instance, the term "zone of responsibility" for the brigades?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that term either area or zone of responsibility will be found in the 1983 command and staff regulations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now -- but in the rules setting up the brigade, is that in the rules?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the brigade rules, you're not going to generally find that, because as a context by which most brigades were designed to fight in the JNA, certainly in 1984, brigades were not generally given a zone of operations or an area of operations, they were normally given something more limited with respect to a frontage, and axis of advance. With respect to brigades, normally within the context of the 1984 regulations, TO units which were given rear service-based operations, counter insurgency, or types of rear missions like that, those units could be given an area of responsibility. But for the actual combat operations, you didn't normally see that at brigade level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, under the rules, if you know, what sort of zones were they given?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally envisioned for the manoeuvre brigades under the 1984 rules, they were derived on a larger military context where a brigade would not necessarily be fighting alone. It was envisioned it would fight as either part of a parent division or when divisions went away and were replaced by a brigade corps structure that they would fight in context with a larger corps formation. So in that context, it was geared towards a more conventional setting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, let me go a little more specific and maybe you can help us out here. In the JNA doctrine, can we consider such things as zone of operation, the area of operation, zone of responsibility as control measures?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that they are some form of control measure, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And if you could tell us, according to the brigade rules what is the mission of an infantry brigade as you understand it to be?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just a time frame, which decade, which war? Are we talking VRS or JNA here?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This is totally uncalled for by the Prosecutor. I'm dealing with an expert; those are the issues that we dealt with last week. Now we're getting flip and irrelevant comments from the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The gentleman understands what I'm talking about, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think the problem of your question is too broad. You may ask a specific question which is relevant to our case. Of course, there is a lot of questions that we could put to this witness, but what we want to hear is the most relevant part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But, Your Honour, I refer -- I understand. That's why I referred to the brigade rules.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, were the brigade rules in effect during this period of time that we're talking about, that is July 1995?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, they were applied, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "for the most part," do you mean that they had discarded some parts?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, with respect to not necessarily discarding, however there are going to be some discrepancies, like, for example, 1984, the role and function of a political officer was envisioned and integrated into the brigade, and obviously you don't have those in 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would be an addition?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that would be -- they rerolled that function to the assistant commander for morale, legal, and religious.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, so for the most part --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this respect one of the things I note with the 1984 regulations is most of the discussion in that is with respect to traditional brigade level military functions, attack, defence, delay, withdraw, and the various types of operations that a brigade conducts in what I would call either a high-, medium-, or low-intensity environment. So in that respect, the regulations lay out those types of functions and activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, during this period, 1995, are you able to tell us what was the mission of the infantry brigades, and of course we're going to be talking about the Drina Corps, so if you could explain that to us, as you understand it to be and in light of the rules that were in place for them to be guided by.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to 1995 in the zone of the Drina Corps, most of the brigades were organised as either light or infantry brigades. There was only one brigade which was organised, notionally at best, as a motorised brigade. Most of the brigades in the Drina Corps zone at that time, their primary mission was defensive in nature. In most cases, particularly around Gorazde, Zepa, and Srebrenica, most of the defences, as well as some of the other areas, were what we could call static defence, just literally manning established defensive positions and repelling any offensive moves by the enemy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I understand you correct, at this point in time prior to the attack on Srebrenica, the Bratunac Brigade is in a static position?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their primary mission would be static defence around the Srebrenica enclave or their portion of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And is that a zone of defence that you -- would you characterise the way it was formed or the way the battalions were laid out, would that be a zone of defence, a zone of responsibility, what would you call that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two perhaps complementary definitions. Within the -- the Bratunac Brigade had an established zone of responsibility. Each of its battalions had a designated defence line. The two were not overlapping. For example, the zone of the Bratunac Brigade was not completely and solely defended by units subordinate to the Bratunac Brigade. There were other formations from other brigades that were performing some defensive functions in there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By that what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the zone of -- that had been established by the Drina Corps for what the brigade's area of responsibility was, there were elements of I believe one battalion of the Milici Brigade, and I believe almost half of the Skelani Separate Battalion would be operating in areas that are covered as supposedly part of the Bratunac Brigade zone from that 1992 map graphic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So -- I mean, I want to make sure that I understand you correctly. Are you saying these other brigades are functioning within the zone of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Elements of outside units were, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not full brigades, but elements of outside units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is why they were still under their own commands?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understand you, within one zone of responsibility you can have overlapping elements of brigades working?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So I take it if they were in the Bratunac Brigade zone of responsibility, commander of the Bratunac Brigade could give them orders as well?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, they're in his zone. Why can't he say: I think you guys ought to move over to this location as opposed to being where you are. We've got incoming, why don't you be the shield, take the brunt of the fighting? It's his zone.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those same control measures that in many respects delineate unit orders, also delineate and articulate what the chain of command is going to be. The fact that units of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade, the Birac Infantry Brigade, the Romanija Brigade were operating in the Bratunac Brigade zone as part of Krivaja 95, certainly it's never been my position that they are de facto under the Bratunac Brigade because they are operating in his zone. That would not be a policy that the VRS itself followed either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To be sure I understand you correctly, because I hadn't gotten to the attack on Srebrenica, maybe you're a little ahead of me. What I want to know is whether they were operating within the zone prior to this order of Krivaja 95?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding is that certainly Tactical Group Pribicevac had been operating in and around that zone since the establishment of the safe area, and it was disbanded sometime in mid-June 1995. And I believe that from the map positions of one battalion of the Milici Brigade, they were -- had defensive positions in a zone that was identified as part of the Bratunac Brigade and they maintained those for several years as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Just to make sure -- I'm trying to get a handle on all of these facts here, so help me out. We're talking about something different than, say, the 4th Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade which was -- which originated from Zvornik but had been attached to and presumably under the direction of the Bratunac Brigade. We're talking about two different concepts here?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. For example, with one battalion of the Milici Brigade operating in the Bratunac zone, my understanding of their system, and again I have no data that says otherwise, that battalion would still be under the command of the Milici Brigade. So it is different in that respect. The 4th Battalion was physically placed under the command of the Bratunac Brigade, but in this particular battalion of the Milici Brigade, they were not put under Colonel Blagojevic's or his predecessor's command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said: "My understanding of their system." You just piqued my interest a little bit. What system are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The general practice that they used or the VRS used when they resubordinated units from one brigade or one area of the country to another for a particular series of circumstances.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But if I understand you correctly, based on what you just told us, because now you're interjecting the word "resubordinated" units. So if I understand you correctly, these units that were there, as you've indicated, were still under the command of their brigades, yet they are operating in somebody else's backyard, somebody else's zone of responsibility. So they were not subordinated, they were not attached, but you're saying "resubordinated". Now, are you suggesting that they were resubordinated to the Bratunac Brigade at that period?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am saying that the 4th Battalion was resubordinated -- the phrase that I don't like to use is attached because it's a Western phrase that doesn't have a common parallel in the JNA doctrine to my knowledge. But the 4th battalion was, in fact, resubordinated from the Drina -- from the Zvornik Brigade. And in that respect, they're under the command of the Bratunac Brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm with you there.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: But with respect to other formations --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Without formal resubordination, certainly a unit of the Milici Brigade would not be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And that's what I'm trying to understand here. Because you said "in their system" and then you interjected "resubordination". Earlier you told us they were operating on their own, hence they're not resubordinated. They're on their own under their own command operating in another brigade's zone of responsibility. So my question was, and it's a simple one: When you say "their system," what system? Because the follow-up question gives you a clue on where I'm going. Where are those rules so I could look at them?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The issue with resubordinations -- is that what we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no, we're not talking about that. I thought we covered that, because they're not resubordinated. We're going to have a whole discussion on resubordination; we'll get to that. I just want to know -- okay. We know about the 4th Battalion. They came from the Zvornik, they were attached -- resubordinated is the correct term of art to the Bratunac Brigade. They're under now the command of the Bratunac Brigade. Okay. We understand that. There may have been some deviations, in fact, even with that, but never mind --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection to the testimony, Your Honour. There's no question here and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm trying to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think Mr. Karnavas is just trying to explain what's in his mind, what his question means.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So now we're not talking about resubordination. Now I'm trying to focus you on this very narrow aspect of your testimony where you said that - and you've said it repeatedly here - that other units from other brigades were operating in the zone of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade, while at the same time being under the control and direction of their own command, which means their own brigade. Okay. Now, that's what you said. So my -- then I asked you -- because you said "their system." So my question is: What system are you referring to? Are we talking about regulations? Are we talking about orders? Are we talking about rules? And again, we're talking about pre-Srebrenica, because I don't want to mix the two.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this context, and now I understand your question, the basis is the 1983 command and staff regulations and the various documents which reflect the practical applications of those during the course of the war from 1992 to just before Srebrenica, since you don't want to go there yet, where there will be a number of orders and documents which again define those command relationships.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I know in Srebrenica we have Krivaja 95, we have directive 7.1, we have a battle plan or battle order, however we want to call it, from the corps from the brigades, and then the brigades have their own orders as to what everybody will do. But prior to Srebrenica, are you telling us now that there are specific command and staff regulations that allow -- and here I'm reading 1983 command and staff regulations, that allow for units of one brigade to be operating in the zone of responsibility - we're going to cover that - the zone of responsibility of another brigade while still maintaining their command of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1983 command and staff regulations do not envision that as a normal practice. The normal practice is that when a battalion or other formation goes into that brigade, it is, in fact, resubordinated to it. The practices that I'm referring to are the ones that we see in the context of the practical series of orders that come out of the context of the VRS orders from 1992 to 1995 where there are instances where units are sent to operate in other areas and zones of responsibility and are not put under the command of the parent brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is -- are these are -- in these instances, is there battle activity going on or are they in a static defence, as you indicated, situation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the course of 1992 to 1995, it was situation-dependant. In some cases, they may well have been conducting offensive operations. Certainly with respect to the Drina Corps by mid-1994, most of the operations were defensive in nature, although, there were limited operations with respect to the enclave at Gorazde that continued to the end of December 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I take it, based on your answer, if we went back to the 1983 regulations that you've just indicated that us, we would not be able to find anything in there, would we, that would say that one unit from one brigade could be operating independently on its own in another brigade's zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that context, I don't think you'd find anything, because it was not envisioned in 1983 that that would be a circumstance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could we say that at least if that was happening on the ground, that was, for all intents and purposes, a deviation from the JNA rules?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. It was a -- it was one of the things that even the JNA recognises, the fact that practical combat experience over the time was going to cause the rules to change. That's why many of the rules are annotated as provisional to allow them to come into their final form on the basis of other experience.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just trying to figure this out. Because You've told us they took the regulations, you see, and they're implementing these regulations, all right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As much as practicable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As much as practicable. But this -- you read my next question. Is this a minor deviation or would you call this a medium or major deviation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's circumstance-dependant. I don't know that I could throw a broad category out there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did give us sort of a broad statement that they, the JNA more or less adopted the organisational structure and the operating methodologies of the VRS. In fact, I find it here in your narration. This is what you say. Here we come at a juncture where it would seem to me, I'm not a military man, but it would seem to me having a unit operate independently in somebody else's zone of responsibility could be of a major concern, such as fratricides, one troop where they get friendly fire or, for instance, one -- the commander of that zone might not wish to have those operating in his zone, may try to give them direction or throw them out. So my question is: Is this a minor deviation which would conform with your analysis that is in your narrative or is this something that, because of the circumstances, is a major deviation, but they just didn't get around to formalising it in their own regulations because of the war?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe that -- within the context of the examples that you've given I'm not even sure within that context it even qualifies as a deviation. Certainly within the context of the JNA rules, there are provisions where select units will operate in another unit's area or zone and reconnaissance units may well fall into that in many cases. And all of the things that you've mentioned, friendly fire, fratricide, the fact that a commander might not know are all valid concerns, and those are concerns that are presumably addressed by the superior command when they direct those orders. The general practice, certainly during the VRS in the war, because we did ask this type of question to many of these officers, was that particularly in the case of some specialised reconnaissance units, they would be aware that the units would be operating in zone, but they wouldn't necessarily be aware what their specific missions were. They would just be informed that these units would be operating in a zone during this time, in this geographical area. And again as part of the control measures issues, all of those are defined by superior command, all within the parameters that you have listed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Just one last question. I think we're about time for a break. That leads me to think now that if they're in somebody else's zone of responsibility and the commander of that zone of responsibility - we haven't tied that down yet, that issue of zone - but it would seem that me that that commander could not be held responsible for the activities and the conduct of those who are operating in his zone of responsibility of whom he has no control over?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's absolutely fair, sir. I believe that is exactly the context of what I've noted. The geographic proximity in a zone is not a measure of command. Command and command relationships are defined by the superior. The fact that a unit from one formation or brigade is located in the zone of operations of another brigade is certainly not a de facto link of command. I don't believe I've ever said it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're just having a conversation, Mr. Butler. There's no accusations being launched.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could we have a break, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Now it's time to have a break and resume at 10 minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Butler, if we could just kind of finish up this little topic before we go on. I take it from your answers that, and correct me if I'm wrong, based on what we were discussing earlier, if I could pose a hypothetical, that Colonel Obrenovic, for example, when he was a lieutenant colonel at the time, or he might have been a major. Obrenovic, for example, within his zone of responsibility he would not have been able unilaterally to remove a unit from the corps or the Main Staff that was in and/or operating within his zone if such a unit had not been subordinated or resubordinated to the Bratunac Brigade. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You mean the Zvornik Brigade --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The Zvornik Brigade, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm using a neutral party as an example.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure if the subordination or resubordination issue is the key trigger on that hypothetical. I believe it's more along the lines of the purposes and what the superior command has designated that unit to be there. I don't -- it's an odd situation. Would he be able to force a unit out that wasn't subordinated to him. If it was subordinated to him, why would he force it out? I don't know if it works that way. The key phrase on this particular one is going to go back to: What would be the purpose by which the superior command designated the unit to be there? So whether it's subordinate or not to Obrenovic, I'm not sure that that matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I agree with you. I thought I would just throw that in. So the answer is he would not be able to throw a unit out of his zone of responsibility if that unit was there as a result of an order by the corps or the Main Staff. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the unit was there by the direction of the superior command, in this case corps or Main Staff, no, Colonel Obrenovic would not be able to, to use your words, throw it out or direct it to leave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or remove them.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: His obligation in that respect would be he would have to go back to the superior command that put them there, either the corps or Main Staff, and either requested that they be withdrawn or whatever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He could not order them around either?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, without knowing the issue of the specifics of their presence there, as directed by the superior command, I don't know the answer to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well -- okay. Maybe my hypothetical was too wide. In this instance, the Zvornik Brigade and the commander at the time, which would have been, say, Mr. Obrenovic. He does not have any particular orders himself, but there is a unit that is placed within his zone of responsibility by the Main Staff or the Drina Corps. So my question is, or rather, I'm stating and I'm asking you to verify it and validate it. In that hypothetical, Mr. Obrenovic would not be able to give those units directions, be it to leave the zone of responsibility or carry out a particular task. He could not engage them in any way, could he?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection as to relevancy to the Zvornik Brigade and if this is meant to be something in particular to the Bratunac Brigade, I have no objection to a hypothetical based on particular facts that we can see in our case, otherwise it's left to speculate what he's really talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think you have made your point already.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is it necessary for --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I take it if the President and the Trial Bench is satisfied that the point has been made, I'll move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now -- that leaves me with fewer questions. But just one minor clarification, I guess. I had asked you earlier about deviation of doctrine from the JNA to the VRS. And I said, well, was this a minor deviation or would it have been a minor deviation. And I believe -- well, I wasn't quite sure what your answer is. But I thought we could revisit what you testified in the Krstic case with respect to this issue. So if we could have Mr. Usher help us out here and if I could show you page 5.284 of your testimony dated 19 July 2000. And it's line 4 --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we have copies of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Are we going to get copies? I think that would be the general courtesy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I will put it on the ELMO so everybody could see, Your Honour. Otherwise, I would have to copy -- I don't mind copying the one page, but I don't want to be responsible for copying the entire transcript. I think we can follow along. It's only six lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, let's put it on the ELMO so that everybody could follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I apologise. In the future I'll make copies for everyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're asked a question:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The doctrine of the Army of Republika Srpska, did it differ from the doctrine of the former JNA?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: My analysis of the doctrine as it evolved from 1992, when the VRS formed out of the remnants of the JNA in Bosnia, through 1995 indicates that there were no major substantive changes with regard to command and control and organisational structure. Now, clearly there were probably a number of minor changes that occurred as a result of the learned experience from combat in the prior three years. Do you recall being asked that question and do you recall giving that answer?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it you would agree with me, would you not, that command and control, for instance, the words that you are using here, which are a term of art, are part of doctrine, are they not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are part of both the broader doctrine and they are part of the more specified regulatory basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And that would -- your answer would apply equally to the terms that you use, "organisational structure"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only change in organisational structures, to my knowledge, occurred sometime in mid-1994 when the -- some units of the VRS were starting to adopt the brigade structure that the VJ was adopting at that time. But within the basis of the larger organisational structure, they tried to remain as faithful to that as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But I guess my question, and I raised it inartfully, the concept of organisational structure is also part of doctrine?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a broader sense, yes, sir, because how you train your personnel and what equipment there is available or how you manufacture that equipment in the larger doctrinal sense revolves around the structure, the organisational structure, you intend on filling. So that is, I think, the relationship there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, getting back to my earlier question, if you could, is it your testimony that giving the brigades a zone of responsibility, was that a minor change?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe in the context, it qualifies as one of those changes that were made as a basis of the combat experience from 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I guess my question was fairly specific. Would you consider that a minor change, a medium-sized, major? What would you consider it, in light of what is being tasked now to the brigades, assuming that we are to accept your narrative that the brigades were given a zone of responsibility, albeit it is not found in the regulations, in the rules?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that it wasn't generally found in the rules. I said that with respect to the TO units, there are mentions where for those type of rear security operations you will find designated areas or zones of operations. But answering your larger question, within the fundamental context of command and control and applications of combat activities, I don't believe that the fact that brigades, for support and infrastructure, were being tied to municipalities which corresponded with zones of operation was a major change, certainly not in combat doctrine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But just to make sure that I understand, are you suggesting that in the brigade rules there is a term that the brigades are assigned zones of responsibility? Is that your understanding? I'm talking about 1984.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding is in the context of the discussions with respect to light infantry brigades, which under the JNA structure at the time were normally found in TOs, that there will be references there that they can be given a zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now -- we're going to get to that. But, you see, I use zone of responsibility, and then we're going to talk about your definition of that. And I want a very clear answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. This is argumentative. It's just simple argument.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Karnavas, just put your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the rules, will we find, be it for light brigade or regular brigade, will we find in the rules such a thing as a brigade having a zone of responsibility, especially in the context in which you have used it in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you won't find that in the brigade rules within the context of a zone corresponding to a municipality boundary. So in this context you won't find that phrase specifically articulated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Will you find in the rules a zone that more or less fits your definition of what a zone of responsibility is, but just lacks the word "responsibility"? In other words, we could read it, we could understand it, it's just not articulated there, the word "responsibility"?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but do you mean all the rules or are you still on the brigade rules?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand the tactics, I know them well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No. I think it's a reasonable question --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're talking about the same rules, the brigade rules, we're on the brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: That's enough. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So staying with me on the brigade rules, I haven't switched off. Are you with me?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am with you, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, on these rules, will we find some language that would give these brigades a zone that would include the definition of a zone of responsibility that you have given?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think you will find a direct correlation. I think it will be an indirect one with respect to the brigade rear area definitions in that context.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, but in your context, sir -- maybe we should look at what your context is. Maybe you could tell us again, and I have what you said, and maybe if there's any discrepancy, we can talk about it. So in your -- what is your understanding that a zone of responsibility is for a brigade?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to the brigade rules or with how we see it in VRS?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, how you see it. Because you already said they're not in the rules.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to the VRS, one of the phenomenon that occurs that 1992, since many, if not most, of the brigades, certainly the light infantry ones, the genesis of those units, or the nucleus, are TO organisations that existed in May of 1992 in each municipality. And what occurred over time as these TO organisations were amalgamated into brigades and then later the army, what you saw within the general context of the VRS and Drina Corps specifically was that a brigade would generally be given a zone of responsibility that in many cases corresponded roughly to the existing boundaries of the municipality. In that respect, it wasn't necessarily command and control-related functions. Certainly in 1992 the primary motivator behind much of that, and in 1993, was that the municipal organisations had a very large role in providing support, personnel, and even in some cases some military equipment to that unit. So the trend that we see from 1992 on is that there will be this association between the brigade and the municipality which the bulk of its troops come from. Hence, even the names, why you have a Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, a Vlasenica Light Infantry Brigade, the association with their parent municipality. That is the context by which I understand these zones of responsibility were organised in the beginning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, is that understanding based on the rules or is it based on your discussions with the interviews of the people that were interviewed, suspects and witnesses, documents, regulations? What is this understanding based on?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This particular understanding for the VRS in 1992 is based upon the documents, interviews, the map graphics, those things that we have which specifically designate the zones as well as the interviews and discussions with these officers who explained how they formed in the first place and why.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So we have the rules, and by your own admission - and we can go through them together - they don't give a zone of responsibility to a brigade. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not envisioned as such in the 1984 rules, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's not in the rules, is it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, as I said, I believe it's there indirectly. With respect to light brigades and rear areas, it does not specifically say it directly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say indirectly, indirectly if we were to look at the particular segment which I'm sure you are going to point us out to, it would correspond with a definition that you gave us that their zone of responsibility or the area of responsibility would roughly correspond the borders that were in the existence -- the rough municipality borders. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, that's my whole point.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you're specifically linking it to a municipality border, then there's no reference as such.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's why I asked you what your definition was, your definition, Butler's definition --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That's argumentive; he's telling him why he's asking him questions. This goes no where but to further argument and helps nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, just put your questions. That's simple enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the context of your definition, Butler's definition, can we find such a definition, either it be direct or indirect, in the rules?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, linking it to municipality borders, there's no such reference.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So the answer is no?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that instance, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, now that you've told us a little bit about the zone of responsibility, could you describe to us where it is, in the rules at least, that we could look at to determine the responsibilities of a brigade commander within the zone of responsibility that -- could you help us out there.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The responsibilities of the brigade commander are delineated in the regulations under the aspects of command. The identification of a particular zone or area of responsibility is not listed in those regulations insomuch as a formal zone. However, again going back to the issues of the light infantry brigade and rear security type of operations, my definition of what those jobs and functions are, you will have language with respect to the issue of what a commander's roles and responsibility are. Now, I would also say that with respect to the responsibilities of the commander and the staff, you can't look at the 1984 regulations in isolation, you have to read them in conjunction with the 1983 command and staff regulations, which do discuss in a broader context these areas of responsibility or zone of responsibility and what a commander is or is not expected to be aware of occurring there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Hold it, hold it now. I'm a little confused. A commander is -- we've already indicated and established that in the rules there's nothing about a zone of responsibility --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, but he's now -- Mr. Butler has referred to another set of rules. If we can just be specific to the rules, the record will be a lot clearer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I haven't asked a question, Your Honour, again if we're going to engage in these tactics, I should be allowed to engage in them as well, interrupting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think we know what you are talking about, so just put your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm attempting, Your Honour. I'm attempting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where could I look to, Mr. Butler, concretely in writing to find where it defines the responsibilities of a brigade commander for a zone of responsibility of a brigade? Just tell me where.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've indicated, if you read the 1984 regulations and read the 1983 regulations, I believe the answer is there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can pull page numbers, if you want, this evening, I would be happy to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I would be happy, because I would like to know exactly where in the regulations itself it talks about responsibilities of a brigade commander within a zone of -- within a zone of responsibility, not a zone of operation, not a zone of defence, but a zone of responsibility. And I take it it is your understanding that we will find concrete language that says that a brigade commander has the following responsibilities when he is the commander of this zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. Now you've misconstrued it, because the brigade commander is a commander of the brigade, he is not the commander of a zone of responsibility. There's no such animal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, that's what I was trying to get at.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The responsibilities of a unit are listed in a zone. The responsibilities of a commander are listed and you have to couple the two. But what you've asked, like I said, there's no such animal in this context.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the 1984 rules do provide us some guidance as to what a brigade is supposed to be doing. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1984 rules - let me just wait a second - define or are the regulatory basis for the responsibilities of the brigade, the commander, the command staff under various or in various wartime situations. So, I mean, that's where you will find the guidance as to what the brigade and by consequence the brigade commander and his staff are doing under various circumstances.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if we were to look at the brigade rules, and maybe if you could pull them out. Do you have them handy?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe they have been marked for identification purposes as P83. If we could look at -- I believe these are paragraphs, not rules, as I've been told by the Prosecution. So if we could look at page 6 at the bottom, that is marked as paragraph number 13, which is under topic 2, assignment, zone of operation and grouping of forces. Do you have it, sir?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Matter of fact, I even have it highlighted, apparently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're thinking alike. Now, what does that state, sir? Does it not state that a brigade is always assigned a zone of operation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, it says "shall".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well "shall". Exactly, but what does "shall" mean? That's my whole point, it must have, it "shall". Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. "Shall" is generally -- I'll take your point that "shall" in this case is a mandatory issue, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please pause.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So it says: "A brigade shall be assigned a zone of operations in which to carry out its tasks," and then it lists the tasks. Zone of attack, zone of defence, zone of march and such like. Now, it would seem to me they are going from the general to the specific. And the general is that they're assigned a zone of operation, not a zone of responsibility, but a zone of operation. Would you agree with me on that point?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. This is what the 1984 regulations specify.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And that one of those zones within the zone of operation is the zone of defence. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must be missing it here. Zone of operations carries out combat operations. I don't know if it specifies defence. I'm missing it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll read it again. It says: "A zone shall be assigned, a zone of operations in which to carry out its tasks."

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "A zone of attack, a zone of defence." It would seem at least the way it's written that under the umbrella of zone of operations comes the zone of defence.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's one of the functions that are conducted in zone, yes, sir. I don't know if it's an umbrella, but yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So -- now, what is a zone of operation in your understanding of the rules?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as it's listed on the ELMO, again it's what we've discussed as control measures or a series of control measures, designated and where the brigade -- where -- and again the designated space where the brigade organises and carries out its combat operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Is that a geographical region?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends. It -- certainly the borders are normally fixed by geographic markers, but if you have a situation where a brigade is operating as part of a larger corps formation, that zone is going to be designated by other operational factors. For example, in the attack, a brigade may have a zone of operations or a front as narrow as 2 to 3 kilometres, where in the defence it may go up ideally to 10 to 15 kilometres. So it is situation-dependant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now -- but as I understand it, earlier you testified, at least with respect to the Bratunac Brigade it was a static defence. Now, could we glean from that anything, that they had a zone of defence or that their zone of operation was where they were located?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their defensive lines, at least the length of them, would be the distance and depth of its four battalions that were on line. As I've noted before, certainly in the case of the Bratunac Brigade the available forces were nowhere near enough to cover the entire zone that was specified for them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we say "zone," are we talking about --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about that map graphic which indicated what their zone of operations was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, are you saying zone of operations, I want to stay consistent. So I'm talking about the line of defence that they had.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can we agree on a particular term. Is that the zone of operation, because it does seem to have a particular length, a width, a depth, you know, so much -- far forward, so far backwards.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In context again to recognise that it's not just the static line, that there is depth forward and behind for the battalions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. How much forward would it go?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, that's situation-dependant and those things are regulated by the superior. There's no set formula to that, at least to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge. And how far backwards?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I believe this is -- there is actually a fixed distance, depending on whether the battalion is in the attack or in the defence. I believe it is in the regulations. I don't remember what it is offhand. I believe there are some fixed criteria to use on that one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, as I understand your testimony correctly that the Bratunac Brigade did not have enough manpower to cover its designated tasks in operating that line and holding that line?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And as I understand you, their responsibilities would have been for a certain distance forward and a certain distance backward. Correct?
