utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. As well as, of course, the linear distance of the line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Exactly. Now, if we take your definition of the zone of responsibility, now we have a situation where a brigade which can hardly line itself up to form this defensive static line, but now under your definition they would also have to be responsible for a geographical region the size of the municipality of Bratunac. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that the phrase "responsibility" is something that I've used in context with that zone. It is its designated zone. I do not have a document from the headquarters of the Drina Corps which articulates the specific roles and responsibilities of a -- of the brigade in that zone in its entirety, so I just don't know I can answer that question for you. Certainly, I don't mean to imply and I hope I never have that the Bratunac Brigade's limited forces at its disposal were somehow expected to man a linear defence line across the entire zone it was given. Most VRS formations could not do the same as well. I think it's an apples and oranges type of issue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But we're not even talking just a linear line. We're also talking the entire geographical region of the -- the boundaries of the municipality, according to your definition.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe I have ever implied that there was a static defence requirement for that. Certainly I wouldn't anticipate them having to garrison that type of a line. I don't believe I've ever said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. But I'm not asking for them to be lined up throughout the entire border, but what I'm saying is one of their tasks throughout that period - and correct me if I'm wrong - was to be stationed and positioned at a particular line where you had the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th Battalion. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they had been there for years. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With minor deviations, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With minor deviations, but by and large the situation was relatively stable, and I use the word "relatively" because there weren't any major battle activities. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir -- it's correct, yes. No major battle activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Up until the time that we get to Srebrenica. Now -- so they were there, but under your definition they would have to be responsible not only for those current duties, which according to you they were undermanned and under-resourced to maintain in a static situation, but also they would have to be responsible for a geographic region the size of the entire municipality, something which was not even envisaged in the rules themselves. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well again, Mr. Karnavas, not knowing what the Drina Corps command envisioned in designating those zones, other than where we see the municipality providing logistics support, I don't know that I can answer the question. Certainly they were undermanned and under-resourced. I believe that even in Colonel Blagojevic's report he says that on 4 July, he makes that point to the Drina Corps. So in that respect -- certainly those instances were not envisioned when the 1984 brigade rules were created.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you have an opportunity to review Mr. Obrenovic's testimony when he testified here?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I reviewed it. I believe I have read the entire series of it once. I haven't reviewed it in detail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And -- okay. Now, if you may recall, and if you don't it doesn't matter because we could help you out here. There were some questions with respect to zone of operation and how it's defined to a particular brigade from the corps and downwards. Do you recall my asking a series of questions regarding that issue?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. That's not familiar to me. I may have read it and I'm just not picking up on it, so if you could help me out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will. If we could put on the ELMO the testimony. It's pages 2.716 and 2.717. If we could start with line 6 -- well, actually we could start with line 11 and read a little bit less than we need to. But if you look at line 8, I'm making a reference to paragraph 13 of the rules, of the brigade rules. So line 11 I start with: "Now, the zone of operation for the brigade is a ground space of limited width and depth, in which a brigade organisations and carries out combat operations. Is that correct?" His answer is: "Yes." Do you agree with him on that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is straight out of the language of paragraph 13. That is correct, sir. Q.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who designates that ground space of limited, limited width and depth? What designates that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The corps command does. Would you agree with him on that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is consistent with the corps command who designates those.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the answer is yes?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Q.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On what basis in that designated? I mean, what are the criteria? I mean, if you know. That they would look at and say: Okay, to the Bratunac Brigade, given the fact that they only have so many soldiers and we need to cover this amount of territory, given that they have this neighbor and that neighbor, with these sorts of resources. What are the criteria?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, as you probably know, I never worked in a corps command, but I can use the experience gained from the brigade command when designating regions for the battalion's defence, the brigade command would then have in mind first of all the composition and combat capabilities of the unit concerned, that is the battalion, and secondly, the geographical characteristics of the terrain on which combat operations are to take place; and third, the expected predicted enemy forces in the ground space concerned, the communications, roads, obstacles, and similar features. Perhaps the corps command would think along those lines. It's an operational command. I've never worked there and I don't have any experience in that respect. And then I go on. Just for completeness I say: "I think that covers it, and I think you might also throw in mission, because you've indicated number of soldiers, equipment, the terrain, the enemy disposition and capability, and I take it also the mission." Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. That is a very good example of the factors that a superior command takes into account when designating that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And that's when designating a zone of operation. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you would agree with me that a zone of operation is more narrowly defined geographically at least than a zone of responsibility that you have given us the definition of to encompass the entire borders of a municipality?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This definition is far more limited and reflects the straight military definition of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's consistent with the rules?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is consistent with the rules, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I -- okay. So it's consistent with the rules and it would seem to be that within this context of the rules that we then come to what you've indicated to us, that if those were the responsibilities of the Bratunac Brigade under its zone of operation and they were maxed out, then surely we could only conclude that if we had your definition as to his zone of responsibility, certainly within that context it would have been virtually impossible to carry out his mission, whatever that may have been.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would disagree only insomuch as, one, again not knowing the mission; but two, while in isolation, it is a significant problem, certainly for the Bratunac Brigade. I just have to go back and say that these problems were consistent throughout all of the problems -- all of the Drina Corps and for the larger part of the VRS as well. It is certainly not an enviable situation that any military professional wants to find themselves in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But we do know the mission of the Bratunac Brigade; it's mission, as you've indicated, was to have a static defence on that particular line because they were in essence facing the 28th Division that was within the enclave under the protection of the UN. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. And in that aspect of their mission, they performed adequately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the Zvornik as well, they had to worry about the 2nd Corps facing them in that direction. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this was their mission, and that mission changed at some point when Krivaja 95 came in and there was an order from the Drina Corps, I believe it's dated the 2nd of July. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. The preparation order and the execute order are dated the 2nd.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So at that point it would seem that a new mission is given to this particular brigade as well as to the other units that ultimately became involved in the attack on Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So now we do know their mission, and their mission, is it not - and correct me if I'm wrong - relatively, the mission for the Bratunac Brigade, relatively the same, even during the attack on Srebrenica, albeit I believe it was the 3rd Battalion that played a -- somewhat of a role and an offensive role. And I know I'm generalising, but -- and we'll get to that, but if you could answer the question.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, generally speaking, that's correct. The specifics are designated in the Bratunac Brigade plan of 5 July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And in fact -- and that order remains in effect for the Bratunac Brigade, does it not, until after they received their next order. And it would appear, at least from the documents that we have, that that next order was received on the 13th. I believe it was one of your exhibits. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In context, the written orders, there was the 5 July written order, which designated or kicked off for the brigade Krivaja. There were some supplemental orders, of course, the 10 July one with respect to mobilisation. Then 13 July, you had Stupcana 95. So in that context with written orders, that's pretty much the main operation orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But can we agree on that for the most part, the Bratunac Brigade from the 5th or 6th when the attack on Srebrenica occurred until its fall on the 13th and going on all the way to the 13th, their position or their orders remained more or less the same as they had received on the 2nd from the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Misstatement of the facts. He may not have meant to say the fall on the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The fall on the 11th but all the way to the 13th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the written orders that were received from the superior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And the orders that they received -- in fact, on the 13th, we see two separate orders, do we not, from two separate commanders of the Drina Corps -- or orders written -- signed by two -- by two different commanders, the one from General Zivanovic and a few hours later, I believe, later in the evening it's around 2100 hours, we see another one from General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think in rough context you're correct there. I think the last order we see from General Zivanovic is approximately 1800 hours that day. So that's the sequence. While he was the corps commander and then after the changeover, the next order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the -- we'll get to them if need be, but the latter order, assuming that General Krstic has now taken command, would I be correct in assuming that that order is indeed the one that's in effect for the Bratunac Brigade and the other units? In other words, does that supersede the previous order received four hours earlier, albeit it's basically the same with some minor changes?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure you can say "superseded". I believe the order that's received from General Zivanovic in this context is the retransmission or the forwarding of that order from the Main Staff with respect to securing roads, mobilising personnel, guarding prisoners, things of that nature. The order from General Krstic specifically articulates sweep operations that are to commence on the morning of the 14th. So like I said, I believe that they work in conjunction. I don't believe that one supersedes the other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that's your interpretation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you say "sweep," and I know this is a habit you have, you like that word, I prefer using the word "search," which is the more correct one as I understand it, but I think we mean the same. Sweep and search is a proper military activity that occurs after a battle, is it not? Am I not correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe we're mixing terminology.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's why I want you to help me out here.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've defined it, my understanding of the JNA terminology in this one, when they talk about what I refer as a sweep operation or what they refer to as clearing the terrain, that is an operation that is conducted when a unit moves down a designated axis in a context where there are no enemy forces left behind. A search operation, as you use the phrase, I don't believe it means the same thing. A search operation can be very simply something that is going over an old battlefield or an area looking for pieces of information or collecting material, things like that. So I think in context, I think sweep operation is the more accurate phrase that we're using.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And then subsequent to the sweep operation, one would expect if there has been battle in that area for asanacija to occur?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally once the area is secured, that would be an expectation, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And those two functions which go hand in glove after an operation are proper military functions?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, they are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's what would be expected in this particular case after the fall of Srebrenica. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this respect, yes. Given the context of the combat operations from the column, it would be a proper military function that the bodies of dead Bosnian Muslim soldiers who were killed in combat would be, in effect, removed from the battlefield and buried in some manner to prevent disease.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And so what we do begin to see on the 14th is an order, do we not, that was drafted by the commander of the Bratunac Brigade that in essence begins to implement what is requested of him by General Krstic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Directed by General Krstic, not requested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. You're correct.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this context he directs three units, the Milici Brigade, the Bratunac Brigade, and the Skelani Battalion to sweep the area of the former enclave and designated zones. And by definition of what we've been talking about, those types of things would be included in that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it you've had an opportunity to then look at the Bratunac Brigade order carrying out the Krstic order?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I believe I discussed that in detail on the Krstic case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it you also had the opportunity to put the map to the order, because that order, if my memory serves me correct, designates with precision on the map where each battalion is supposed to sweep.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct. And again, I think we went through that exercise in the Krstic trial where we actually put it on a map in court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And of course that was a proper military event, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a proper military order within the context, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And carrying out that order was in no way criminal in any way?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that insomuch as I have no visibility on any potential prisoners that may have been taken. The actual function of carrying out that order is certainly not criminal, but I can't say the next step which is that events that occurred pursuant to that may or may not have been criminal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. At that point in time, that is the morning of the 14th, the column was -- had left the Bratunac Brigade area, had it not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the 14th, the column, as I understand it in time, there was still certainly in front of the 4th Battalion's area, there were still sightings of members of the column, the back end of the column was still in that area. But the bulk of the column was already further towards the road - I don't have a map unfortunately - but towards Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have no knowledge of the 1st, 2nd, or 3rd Battalion engaging the column itself, attacking it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In interviews that were conducted by the battalion commanders, they indicate that they did not gain contact -- in those particular cases they did not gain contact with the column, the 1st, the 2nd, and the 3rd.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "gain contact," I take it they didn't come into contact?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. They didn't engage in active combat activity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If I'm correct, if my knowledge of the terrain is right, you have the Bratunac Brigade on one side, you have the Milici Brigade on the other, and there seemed to be some sort of a natural corridor, if I can use that term, that was unmanned -- perhaps there were mines, it was heavily mined, but you had no soldiers of the Bratunac Brigade or the Milici Brigade in there, thus allowing them to go through this corridor towards Zvornik. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the context, there was a gap between the 4th Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade and one of the battalions of the Milici Brigade that was mined, but it was not garrisoned -- they did not have an actual unit there to block the path. And this was the route that the column took.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And no units were sent to block the path?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not -- there is conflicting data on that. I don't have any written orders which indicates that. However, there is some information that a small unit may have been sent to try to get to that area which was Ravni Buljin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But as you've indicated, there was no contact made. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not by the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Battalions, post-14 July with respect to that order. For the most part, they were sweeping the area of the former enclave that had already been evacuated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the 4th Battalion? Are you suggesting - I don't know, I'm asking - that the 4th Battalion actually came into contact and engaged the column?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They came into contact with the column, at least according to some of the interviews of members from that battalion. Depending upon who you talk to, the column, by mutual consent of the soldiers on the ground at the time, was just allowed to pass. Or if you talk to the battalion commander, they didn't see anything. But certainly the 4th Battalion did butt up to part of the column but for whatever reason allowed them to pass relatively unscathed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in other words they did not attack the column?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And it's after they passed through that area that they -- that there is contact between the column and the Zvornik Brigade, and that's where we have casualties, I take it, by both sides. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- well, in time context, the head of the column was already in the Zvornik Brigade area as early as the 13th of July. And by the 13th of July, I mean certainly the back end of the column was still across from the 1st and 4th Battalions. So I think it's an issue of timing on that one. By the 14th, most of the column had already departed what was the former enclave at that time. So I don't know that -- like I said, your analysis with the Zvornik Brigade, the column was long enough that it was engaged at both places at the same time, because parts of it got cut off --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I guess getting back, it's your understanding that the 4th Battalion did not engage the column?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection to vague. He may still be talking about after the 14th, because that was your original question. It's just not clear in terms of time frame from your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm trying to get to is that you have this column that is relatively visible at some point, but they pass through the 3rd, the 2nd, the 1st, and the 4th Battalion relatively unscathed, there is no contact, even with the 4th Battalion. And there is only contact with the column once -- with the Zvornik Brigade once they get into that area. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within context of time on the 14th; however, again our understanding of the context of that is derived from discussions with those members of the battalion. We don't have documents which either confirm or deny that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But at some point, the situation changes on the ground, particularly as a column comes into contact with the Zvornik Brigade. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It changes with context to Zvornik. I think if we're going to stay in the Bratunac area, I believe where the situation changes in context is that by the evening of the 13th of July the VRS defence along the Nova Kasaba, Konjevic Polje, Bratunac route has solidified to a point where certainly during the day and even in the evening hours or periods of darkness, the bulk of the column in numbers can't cross the road from the Bratunac Brigade area to the Zvornik Brigade area in that context. So I think with respect to Bratunac, that's where the situation changes when it comes clear by 13 July that the column is not going to be allowed completely out of the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you said Bratunac Brigade area. Are we talking about a zone? Are we talking about -- well, let me rephrase it. At this point on the 13th, is not the Bratunac Brigade battalions still remaining in their positions where the 1st, the 2nd, the 3rd and the 4th were, are they still not there?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a general context, they are in and around that area. However, as the Trial Chamber is aware, large elements of those battalions are also roaming around Potocari those days as well and conducting more limited operations in and around that area. So that -- for the 2nd Battalion and the 3rd Battalion certainly they are a significant distance away from their former defence lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you said that: "The Trial Chamber is aware that large elements of those battalions," now that really piqued my interest --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, would you please keep your interest to tomorrow. It's time to stop although you still have a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me just ask one question, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Might I ask these large elements, can you give me a numerical figure, and then we'll launch you into a discussion tomorrow about it. But can we have a numerical figure about these large elements that the Trial Chamber is aware of.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have a number. My context of those large elements are the numbers of troops that are seen in the various videos of Potocari on 12 and 13 July. I don't believe that -- say again?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, go ahead. I have a follow-up.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe that in the context of any of the orders there are numbers listed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "troops," you know, are you saying soldiers?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am saying soldiers who I believe the investigation and the Trial Chamber have identified as members of the 2nd and 3rd Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But when you say "troops," as opposed to soldiers, you know, the video had soldiers, now you're talking troops.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm conjuring up Afghanistan, Iraq, that's what I'm conjuring up. So when you say"troops" --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will be specific.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Soldiers from the Bratunac Brigade in those videos.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will reserve the rest of my cross on this area for tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Of course. Of course. I have to remind the parties that next Tuesday will be an UN holiday that we will not be sitting, and it is our hope that we could finish the testimony of this witness by that time. I understand this a very important witness. There are a lot of questions to ask, but I also hope the Defence counsel could streamline somehow overnight their cross-examination for tomorrow and take into consideration the time limits that we are not going to hear the parties about the 92 bis documents. And from the submissions from the parties, I believe that this Bench is in the position to make a ruling on those 92 bis documents. Having said that, I think the hearing is adjourned and we'll meet tomorrow 9.00 in Courtroom III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: at 7.02 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 19th day of November, 2003, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25
